glossary.Heterophile antibody test: Blood test for non-specific antibodies made in EBV infection that clump animal red cells; the monospot is one.
glossary.Tonsillar enlargement: Swelling of the tonsils at the back of the throat.
glossary.Pharynx: The throat behind the mouth and nose, leading down to the oesophagus and larynx.
glossary.Erythematous: Red because of increased blood flow from inflammation.
glossary.Viral hepatitis: Inflammation of the liver caused by a virus.
glossary.Haemodynamic instability: Blood pressure and pulse not maintaining adequate circulation, such as low BP with a fast heart rate.
glossary.Tachycardia: Heart rate above 100 beats per minute.
glossary.Diaphragmatic irritation: Blood or inflammation touching the diaphragm, which refers pain to the shoulder tip via the phrenic nerve.
glossary.Inflammatory markers: Blood tests that rise with inflammation, mainly CRP and ESR.
glossary.Upper airway obstruction: Narrowing or blockage of the nose, throat or larynx that hampers breathing in.
glossary.Gold standard: The most accurate test available, against which others are judged.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: measures haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.Ibuprofen: A non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used for pain, fever and inflammation.
glossary.Contact sports: Sports with body contact or impact, such as rugby or boxing, which risk abdominal trauma.
glossary.Cytotoxic T-cells: CD8+ white cells that kill virus-infected cells.
glossary.Polyclonal B-cell proliferation: Many different B-cell families multiplying at once, rather than one clone.
glossary.Leucoplakia: A white patch on a mucous membrane, such as the inside of the mouth.
glossary.Inspiratory stridor: High-pitched noise on breathing in, caused by narrowing of the upper airway.
glossary.Saliva: Fluid made in the mouth; EBV spreads through it.
glossary.Lymph nodes: Small immune glands along lymph vessels that swell when fighting infection.
glossary.LUQ: Left upper quadrant of the abdomen, where the spleen lies.
